messages:
IncidentBot: PAGER — MERCURY-VPC-RESERVED - Elevated error rate and latency on dedicated pool dp-onyx-1

IncidentBot: Severity: Sev2
IncidentBot: Bridge: https://calls.redwood.com/bridges/xyz789
IncidentBot: Notifying oncall, eng-runtime, ops, and customer-success

Lena (oncall): Joining bridge. Kicking off quick perf checks and process list on dp-onyx-1

Sam: I see a steady increase in 5xxs originating from worker-3 and worker-9. Logs show repeated `oom` then restart on worker-9.

Diego: Worker-9 hosts the enterprise tenant mercury-enterprise (pinned). Checking tenant request distribution and sequence lengths now.

Lena (oncall): Quick query: `metrics.traffic.by_tenant(pool=\"dp-onyx-1\")` -> mercury-enterprise 64% of tokens, with several seqs >3000 in last 10m

Nisha (ops): Confirmed deployment: dp-onyx-1 is reserved capacity with autoscale disabled per account contract. No pre-configured emergency burst lanes.

Rae (customer-success): I'm on the bridge. Mercury SRE (jon) is here — they reported user-facing timeouts affecting API endpoints. They're requesting ETA and whether we'll credit them.

Tom (eng-runtime): Possible noisy tenant long-seqs causing KV cache pressure and swapping, leading to OOMs. Options: evict background jobs, route to degraded quantized model, or free cache. Which first?

Diego: Evicting non-critical rerank jobs safe. Running `kubectl get pods -l tenant=mercury-enterprise,job=rerank` -> scaling down now `kubectl scale deployment/mercury-rerank --replicas=0`

Lena (oncall): Scaled. Observability: CPU on worker-9 dropped 15% but still experiencing swap thrash.

Nisha (ops): We can spin up fallback pool dp-fallback-rt in same AZ but warm time ~9-11 minutes. Could do partial traffic shift (canary) to reduce load immediately while warm completes.

Tom (eng-runtime): Canary routing config prepared: `{"route":{"tenant":"mercury-enterprise","percent":20,"model":"redwood/rw-llama-13b-q4"}}` — ensures metadata preserved. Deploying routing change now.

Lena (oncall): Canary applied. Early metrics: p95 latency for canary ~300ms, errors at 1.2%. Primary still at 14% errors but trending down.

Rae (customer-success): Mercury SRE says the degraded model is acceptable for non-critical endpoints; they want full traffic back after warm.

Sam: I see Redis shard-7 memory usage very high and fragmentation > 80%. Running `redis-cli INFO MEMORY` and scanning for stale prefixes.

Tom (eng-runtime): Suggest deleting untouched prefix entries older than 2h for that tenant. Diego, can you run a safe TTL-based eviction?

Diego: Executing TTL trim script against cache-shard-7: `./scripts/trim-prefix.sh --tenant mercury-enterprise --older-than 7200` -> reclaimed ~7.3GB

Lena (oncall): After trimming cache, OOMs stopped. Worker restarts dropped. 5xx baseline restored to normal within ~18 minutes. Marking as mitigated at 4509877460.

IncidentBot: Incident state -> Mitigated (Customer impact: degradation for ~27 minutes).

Rae (customer-success): Drafting customer update: short summary, root cause, mitigation steps, and offer 4% SLA credit for the impacted window. Will confirm language with legal.

Tom (eng-runtime): Follow-ups for RCA: 1) Root cause: large long-running sequences from mercury-enterprise caused KV cache fragmentation + reserved pool with no burst fallback, 2) Why reserved pool lacked emergency burst configuration, 3) Why TTL eviction didn't auto-trigger — examine cache-trim cron and signal handling.

Nisha (ops): Action items: add an emergency warm pool in each region for reserved deployments, and a pre-approval policy to route <=25% traffic to fallback during warm. I'll add runbook steps including the exact `kubectl scale` and routing commands executed.

Diego: I'll own the short-term change to make cache TTL eviction tenant-aware and ensure the trimming job runs more aggressively when fragmentation >70% for >5m. ETA: 1 week for deploy.

Lena (oncall): I'll write the incident timeline, attach logs, and hand off to next oncall at 11:50. Leaving monitoring watch for 1 hour with alert: errors >2% sustained for 10m -> page SRE and eng-runtime.

Sam: Filing internal suggestion: consider per-tenant circuit breaker that triggers model-level fallback for long-seq patterns.

Rae (customer-success): I'll post the customer note to #customer-comms and circulate the exec one-pager. Also scheduling a joint architecture review with Mercury next Tue.

IncidentBot: Please move RCA drafts to /docs/incidents/4509876500-rca-draft.md when ready.

Nisha (ops): Filing a provisional credit recommendation: 4% for 27 minutes. Adding to the incident ticket for review.

Lena (oncall): Closing bridge. Thanks all for fast coordination — good work.

Diego: ack, monitoring.

Tom (eng-runtime): will start RFC for burst-lane support for reserved pools. Target RFC in 2 weeks.

Rae (customer-success): Mercury appreciated the rapid response; asked if we can include longer TTL for their specific workload as an interim opt-in. I'll capture that as a follow-up.

Lena (oncall): End of thread."
